    compute the mode for their most common rating, and measure standard deviation for
    consistency. For LOW confidence (count < 5), acknowledge prediction uncertainty in
    your reasoning. If std dev < 0.5, the user is highly consistent—predict very close to
    mean. If std dev > 1.0, the user is variable—use mode as primary prediction. If
    distribution is bimodal, favor the mode over mean. Base predictions ONLY on statistical
    evidence. When the user is harsh (mean < 3.0), predict lower ratings. When lenient

    center around their historical mean. For HIGH confidence predictions, use ±0.15 tolerance.
    For MEDIUM confidence, use ±0.25 tolerance. For LOW confidence, use ±0.4 tolerance.
    Strictly adhere to their historical rating average, sentiment polarity, and linguistic patterns.

    rating. If their mean is X.X, your stars MUST be X.X ± 0.2 for typical users, tighter
    (±0.15) for consistent users (std dev < 0.5), and wider (±0.3) for variable users
    (std dev > 1.0). Replicate exact stylistic patterns: if they use ALL CAPS for emphasis,
    preserve that. If they write short one-line reviews, stay brief (under 10 words). If
    they write long detailed reviews, expand accordingly. If they never use emojis, exclude
    them. If they use punctuation patterns (!, ?, ...), match those exactly. Match sentiment
    polarity exactly—negative users remain negative, positive stay positive. CRITICAL:
    Never default to 4 or 5 stars. A user averaging 2.8 must produce ratings between 2.6-3.0.
    Match their review length (±20% word count), vocabulary level, sentence structure
    (simple vs complex), and typical phrases or expressions they use. The analyst's
    prediction is your anchor—deviate only when item context strongly justifies it,
    and even then stay within ±0.3 stars maximum.

  temperature: 0.4
# EVOLVE-BLOCK-END
